beats.subline: Friday, September 11, 2026 close — a choppy, Labor Day-shortened week that ended lower despite a strong Friday rebound.
beats.body: Markets were closed Monday for Labor Day, leaving a four-session week in which an oil-price spike tied to the widening Mideast conflict and caution ahead of the Fed's next meeting drove four straight losing days before Friday's in-line inflation report and a pullback in crude sparked a rebound that trimmed, but didn't erase, the week's declines.

beats.headline: Houthi rebels seize Yemen's Mayun Island, closing off Saudi Arabia's last working oil export route
beats.body: Iran-backed Houthi forces captured the strategic island of Mayun (Perim) in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait on Friday; with the Strait of Hormuz already restricted by the US Navy's blockade and Saudi Arabia's own pipeline shut down as a precaution after an attack, Riyadh is left with no functioning corridor to move its crude, a development analysts say fits Iran's broader strategy of driving up global oil prices to pressure Washington.

beats.headline: Taiwan tracks fresh PLA aircraft and warship activity as Xi prepares to travel to Washington for a September 24 summit
beats.body: Taiwan's Ministry of National Defense detected 5 PLA aircraft sorties and 5 PLAN ships operating around the island as of Saturday morning, with 3 of the sorties crossing into Taiwan's southwestern and eastern air defense zones -- part of the steady drumbeat of Chinese military activity that continues even as Xi Jinping prepares for his second summit with Trump this year.

beats.headline: CENTCOM says its Iran blockade has redirected 100 commercial ships in two months, with zero getting through
beats.body: US Central Command said the 'steel wall' naval blockade against Iranian ports, reinstated July 14, has redirected 100 commercial vessels over the past 60 days and that not a single ship has passed through without US forces' permission, underscoring how central the Navy's enforcement role has become to the broader war's economic-pressure campaign.

beats.headline: Ukrainian sea drone sinks a Russian naval drone in what's being called the first drone-vs-drone naval battle
beats.body: A Ukrainian Sargan-3000 unmanned surface vessel armed with a 12.7mm remote weapons station maneuvered alongside and sank a Russian Orcan-type naval drone in the Black Sea on Saturday, a milestone showing uncrewed platforms now fighting each other directly rather than just striking crewed ships -- a trend the Pentagon is watching closely as it builds out its own unmanned surface vessel programs.

beats.headline: Anthropic's Dario Amodei tells CBS the industry has 'lied' about AI risk, commits to permanent third-party safety audits
beats.body: In a broadcast interview, the Anthropic CEO said AI capability growth is on a curve 'starting to get steeper' -- a warning sign the industry needs to slow down -- and announced Anthropic will give independent evaluators permanent, ongoing access to check its models against stated safety practices, comparing it to food-safety inspection; he also backed federal oversight, including a possible 'kill switch' for dangerous systems.

beats.headline: Rome Odunze played through his calf injury in the opener; Bears turn to a Week 2 home date with Minnesota
beats.body: Odunze, who had been questionable much of last week, suited up for Sunday's season opener at Carolina after NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported he was expected to go; the Bears now shift focus to a Week 2 home game against the Vikings at Soldier Field on Sunday, September 20.

beats.headline: William Byron's Round of 12 continues at Bristol's Bass Pro Shops Night Race on Saturday, Sept. 19
beats.body: Byron's Chase for the NASCAR Cup Series championship moves to the third race of the Round of 12 at Bristol Motor Speedway's concrete half-mile, with the Bass Pro Shops Night Race green-flagging at 7:30 p.m. ET on USA Network, PRN Radio and SiriusXM; Josef Newgarden will drive the Chevrolet pace car for the event.

beats.headline: No fresh news on this beat right now
beats.body: The denomination's recent items -- the September call to prayer and fasting, Fred Greco's confirmation as Stated Clerk, and the creation of two new presbyteries -- were already reported in prior briefs, and no new PCA-specific story surfaced within the 72-hour window today.
